questions.question_text:
A map has a scale of $1:200\,000$.
Two towns are $4$ cm apart on the map.
How far apart are they in real life?

options.why: Converted $800\,000$ cm to kilometres by dividing by $10\,000$ instead of $100\,000$.
Converted $800\,000$ cm to kilometres by dividing by $1\,000\,000$ instead of $100\,000$.
Divided by the scale instead of multiplying, treating the map as the larger of the two.

questions.solution_text:
$4\times200\,000=800\,000\text{ cm}$
$800\,000\div100\,000=8\text{ km}$
The towns are $8$ km apart.

questions.question_text:
A model of a ship is built to a scale of $1:250$.
The real ship is $75$ m long.
How long is the model, in centimetres?

options.why: Converted $75$ m to $75\,000$ cm instead of $7500$ cm before dividing by the scale.
Divided $75$ m by $250$ to get $0.3$ m and then labelled the answer as centimetres.
Multiplied by $250$ instead of dividing, making the model larger than the real ship.

questions.solution_text:
$75\text{ m}=7500\text{ cm}$
$7500\div250=30\text{ cm}$
The model is $30$ cm long.

questions.question_text:
A recipe for $8$ scones uses $240$ g of flour and $60$ g of butter.
How much butter is needed for $20$ scones?

options.why: Scaled the flour by $2.5$ instead of the butter.
Doubled the butter for $16$ scones and ignored the remaining $4$ scones.
Divided $60$ by $20$ and multiplied by $8$, scaling from the new number back to the old.

questions.solution_text:
$20\div8=2.5$
$60\times2.5=150\text{ g}$
He needs $150$ g of butter.

options.why: Multiplied $60$ kg by the $9$ wheat parts instead of dividing by the $12$ total parts first.
Found the millet, $2$ parts, instead of the wheat.
Stopped at the value of one part, which is the sunflower, instead of taking $9$ parts.

questions.solution_text:
$12\text{ parts}=60\text{ kg}$
$1\text{ part}=5\text{ kg}$
$9\text{ parts}=45\text{ kg}$
The batch contains $45$ kg of wheat.

questions.question_text:
Two partners invested $\$9000$ and $\$6000$ in a business.
A profit of $\$25\,000$ is shared in the same ratio as their investments.
How much does the smaller investor receive?

options.why: Gave the larger investor's share of $3$ parts instead of the smaller investor's $2$ parts.
Split the profit equally between the two partners instead of in the ratio $3:2$.
Stopped at the value of one part instead of multiplying by the smaller investor's $2$ parts.

questions.solution_text:
$9000:6000$
$=3:2$
$5\text{ parts}=\$25\,000$
$1\text{ part}=\$5000$
$2\text{ parts}=\$10\,000$
The smaller investor receives $\$10\,000$.

questions.question_text:
Three people share $\$480$.
Ida receives $\frac{1}{4}$ of the money, and the rest is shared between Jo and Kai in the ratio $3:5$.
How much does Kai receive?

options.why: Shared the whole $\$480$ in the ratio $3:5$ without first removing Ida's share.
Gave Jo's share of $3$ parts instead of Kai's share of $5$ parts.
Gave Ida's quarter of the money instead of Kai's share.

questions.question_text:
A house plan is drawn to a scale of $1:150$.
On the plan a rectangular room measures $3$ cm by $2$ cm.
What is the actual floor area of the room, in square metres?

options.why: Scaled each length correctly but converted centimetres to metres by dividing by $10$ instead of $100$.
Multiplied the plan area of $6$ cm$^{2}$ by $150$ instead of scaling each side length first.
Gave the area measured on the plan and simply relabelled the units as square metres.

questions.question_text:
A baker uses $800\text{ g}$ of flour to make 4 loaves.
How much flour will be needed to make 9 loaves?

options.why: Multiplies 800 by 9 without first dividing by the four loaves.
Uses an incorrect scale factor for converting four loaves to nine.

questions.solution_text: Each loaf uses $800\div4=200\text{ g}$. For 9 loaves the amount is $9(200)=1800\text{ g}$.

questions.question_text:
Here are the ingredients for cookies.
How much sugar will be needed to make 20 cookies?
Cookies (makes 5)
60 g butter
70 g sugar
1 egg
90 g flour

options.why: This is not four times the 70 g required for five cookies.
This multiplies the sugar by 20 rather than by the scale factor 4.

questions.solution_text: Twenty cookies is $20/5=4$ times the recipe. Sugar required is $4\times70=280\,g$.
